(This Evening through Saturday)...
Issued at 147 PM EDT Sat Oct 10 2026

The remnants of Hurricane Isaias will lift up the western side of 
the Appalachians through Sunday with light showers overspreading 
most of the forecast area later today through early Sunday morning. 
Upper level ridging will build in immediately as the tropical 
remnants depart...setting the stage for near record breaking warmth 
Monday and Tuesday. Rain chances will return late Tuesday into 
Thursday with the coolest air of the season so far to follow next 
weekend.

Rest of This Afternoon through Sunday Night

Mid and high level clouds associated with Isaias continue to expand 
across the region early this afternoon with the leading edge of 
light rain now into southern Indiana. Temperatures early this 
afternoon were largely in the 70s.

The primary focus in the near term remains on the remnants of Isaias 
and impacts to the area. Trends continue to shift the storm track a 
bit further to the east resulting in lower rainfall amounts for 
central Indiana with growing confidence that much of the northwest 
half may see trace amounts or nothing at best.

Drier air is already being ingested into the weakening system with 
the rain shield approaching from the south gradually diminishing in 
coverage and intensity. By far the greater concern for heavy 
rainfall will reside in the central Appalachians where a persistent 
easterly flow in the lower levels will support upslope flow and 
enhanced rainfall rates coinciding with the deeper moisture plume. 
Across the Ohio Valley...rainfall will be reliant on the remnant 
upper low as it pivots to the northeast tonight. The best chance for 
widespread light rain will come this evening into the early 
overnight and focus across the southeast half of the forecast area 
as an increase in 850mb flow pivots across eastern Kentucky into 
West Virginia and southern Ohio. An attendant band of convergence 
will promote more widespread rainfall but with the lack of deeper 
moisture...amounts will largely remain in the 0.10 to 0.25 inch 
range along and east of I-69 dropping to nothing in the northern 
Wabash Valley. Will also pull any mention of thunder for tonight 
with virtually no instability available. 

The passage of the 850mb jet to the southeast this evening will also 
aid in a period with gusts to 20-25mph focused again primarily 
across the southeast half of the forecast area. Winds will back and 
decrease overnight with any lingering rain ending shortly after 
daybreak Sunday. Lower stratus will develop late tonight and persist 
through Sunday morning as model soundings show moisture within the 
boundary layer trapped beneath an inversion. The trend will be for a 
gradual mixing out of the stratus from the west into the afternoon 
with much drier air advecting into the region as what is left of 
Isaias moves away to the east.

Temps...clouds tonight will keep much of the area in the upper 50s. 
Low level thermals support highs Sunday in the low 70s over eastern 
counties to near 80 in the Wabash Valley.

Monday Through Saturday

Broad upper level ridging will quickly reestablish across the region 
by Monday with stronger southwesterly flow developing between a 
frontal boundary over the upper Midwest and high pressure along the 
Gulf coast. Strong warm advection will commence and result in well 
above normal temperatures for Monday and Tuesday across the region. 
Highs may flirt with 90 degrees in the Wabash Valley on Monday and 
Tuesday. For KIND...record highs of 86 for both Monday and Tuesday 
will be approached. The frontal boundary over the Great Lakes will 
drift south towards the area Tuesday afternoon with the potential 
for isolated convection increasing in coverage Tuesday night into 
Wednesday as the front shifts through the forecast area and 
eventually stalls south of the Ohio River.

An increasingly amplified flow aloft driven by a deep upper low over 
the Rockies will flatten the ridge over the southeast states while 
initiating a significant pattern change for the region by late week 
into next weekend. The aforementioned boundary will remain in a 
quasi-stationary state just south of the forecast area Wednesday 
before pulling back north in response to a surface low ejecting out 
of the Rockies and upper jet phasing. Rain with embedded 
thunderstorms will increase in coverage across the Ohio Valley as a 
result Wednesday night into Thursday before a stronger cold front 
sweeps across the region late week. 

In the wake of the frontal passage...a broad upper trough will 
settle across much of the eastern half of the country as a much 
cooler airmass will overspread the region with strong cold advection 
in place. Highs primarily in the 60s on Friday may struggle to get 
to get out of the 50s over the northeast half of the forecast area 
next weekend. Confidence continues to grow in the first frost of the 
Fall for much of the area next Saturday and Sunday nights as lows
